rule.title: Deletion of Volume Shadow Copies via WMI with PowerShell - PS Script
rule.author: Tim Rauch, frack113

es.summary: Un script de PowerShell consultó la clase WMI Win32_ShadowCopy y la eliminó con .Delete(), Remove-WmiObject o Remove-CimInstance. Suele ser un paso previo al cifrado por ransomware y debe tratarse como incidente potencial.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de Script Block Logging (4104) cuyo ScriptBlockText contiene a la vez un cmdlet de consulta WMI/CIM (Get-WmiObject, gwmi, Get-CimInstance, gcim), la cadena Win32_ShadowCopy y un método o cmdlet de borrado (.Delete(), Remove-WmiObject, rwmi, Remove-CimInstance, rcim).
es.why_it_matters: Borrar las instantáneas de volumen (VSS) impide restaurar archivos y es la técnica ATT&CK T1490, Inhibit System Recovery. Familias de ransomware como Sodinokibi/REvil la usan antes de cifrar o justo después.
triage_steps: Lea el ScriptBlockText completo; si MessageTotal es mayor que 1, reconstruya el bloque uniendo los eventos con el mismo ScriptBlockId.
Identifique el usuario y el proceso PowerShell (Path, ProcessId) y busque su creación en 4688/Sysmon 1 para revisar CommandLine y ParentImage.
Revise el mismo host en +/- 15 minutos: vssadmin delete shadows, wbadmin, bcdedit /set recoveryenabled, detención de servicios de backup o antivirus.
Busque signos de cifrado: renombrado masivo de archivos, extensiones nuevas, notas de rescate o picos de escritura en disco y recursos compartidos.
Verifique si el usuario y el host tienen alertas previas, inicios de sesión inusuales o movimiento lateral (PsExec, WMI remoto, RDP) en las últimas 24 horas.
Confirme con el equipo de infraestructura si existe una tarea de mantenimiento de VSS o una prueba de red team autorizada.
false_positives: Scripts de administradores o software de backup que depuran instantáneas antiguas para liberar espacio.
Pruebas autorizadas de red team o de Atomic Red Team (T1490) en equipos de laboratorio.
Herramientas de aprovisionamiento o limpieza de imágenes que eliminan instantáneas antes de capturar una plantilla.
response_steps: Si no hay justificación confirmada, aísle el endpoint de la red mediante el EDR y deshabilite temporalmente la cuenta implicada.
Preserve evidencia: eventos 4104, memoria y artefactos del script antes de reiniciar o limpiar el equipo.
Busque el mismo ScriptBlockText o hash del script en todo el parque y contenga los otros hosts afectados.
Elimine la persistencia y el acceso del atacante, restablezca credenciales comprometidas y restaure desde backups offline verificados.
es.severity_rationale: Nivel high porque la combinación de consulta y borrado de Win32_ShadowCopy casi no tiene uso legítimo y suele preceder al ransomware.

en.summary: A PowerShell script queried the Win32_ShadowCopy WMI class and deleted shadow copies via .Delete(), Remove-WmiObject or Remove-CimInstance. This commonly precedes ransomware encryption and should be treated as a potential incident.
en.what_it_detects: Script Block Logging events (4104) whose ScriptBlockText contains a WMI/CIM query cmdlet (Get-WmiObject, gwmi, Get-CimInstance, gcim), the string Win32_ShadowCopy, and a delete method or cmdlet (.Delete(), Remove-WmiObject, rwmi, Remove-CimInstance, rcim).
en.why_it_matters: Deleting Volume Shadow Copies prevents file recovery; this is ATT&CK T1490, Inhibit System Recovery. Ransomware families such as Sodinokibi/REvil do it right before or after encrypting.
triage_steps: Read the full ScriptBlockText; if MessageTotal is above 1, rebuild the block by joining events sharing the same ScriptBlockId.
Identify the user and PowerShell process (Path, ProcessId); find its creation in 4688/Sysmon 1 to review CommandLine and ParentImage.
Check the same host within +/- 15 minutes for vssadmin delete shadows, wbadmin, bcdedit recoveryenabled changes, or stopped backup/AV services.
Look for encryption signs: mass file renames, new extensions, ransom notes, or write spikes on local disks and file shares.
Check the user and host for earlier alerts, unusual logons or lateral movement (PsExec, remote WMI, RDP) in the last 24 hours.
Confirm with infrastructure whether a VSS maintenance task or authorized red team test was scheduled.
false_positives: Admin or backup software scripts pruning old shadow copies to free disk space.
Authorized red team or Atomic Red Team (T1490) tests on lab machines.
Imaging or cleanup tooling that removes shadow copies before capturing a template.
response_steps: Without a confirmed justification, isolate the endpoint through EDR and temporarily disable the involved account.
Preserve evidence: 4104 events, memory and script artifacts before rebooting or cleaning the host.
Hunt for the same ScriptBlockText or script hash fleet-wide and contain other affected hosts.
Remove attacker persistence and access, reset compromised credentials, and restore from verified offline backups.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because querying and deleting Win32_ShadowCopy together has little legitimate use and usually precedes ransomware.

positive.description: Atomic-style deletion of all shadow copies with Get-WmiObject and .Delete()
CIM variant using aliases gcim and rcim

negative.description: Inventory script that only lists shadow copies without deleting them

event.ScriptBlockText: Get-WmiObject Win32_ShadowCopy | Select-Object ID, InstallDate, VolumeName | Format-Table

negative.description: Backup script that creates a shadow copy instead of deleting one
